name: US Department of Labor AI Literacy Framework
status: Official US framework with five content areas.

resources.label: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
resources.note: How the organization manages AI risk

foundation_intro: Every session in this plan sits under one of the five foundational content areas in the US Department of Labor's AI Literacy Framework (February 2026).

principles.label: Hands-on, experiential learning
principles.how: Every session includes a 10-minute 'try' step, and the practice sandbox gives instant feedback.

principles.label: Learning embedded in the context of work
principles.how: Practice uses a real task from your own job, with made-up details.

principles.label: Human skills alongside AI skills
principles.how: Reflection, judgment and knowing when not to use AI are part of every plan.

principles.label: Pathways for continued learning
principles.how: The plan ends with a 90-day check-in and points to deeper learning for your role.

principles.label: Designed to change as AI changes
principles.how: All content lives in editable files, so it can be updated as tools evolve.

items: **No federal AI law for employers.** Rules are set by states and cities.
**Illinois:** employees must be told when AI is used in employment decisions, and AI must not discriminate (since January 1, 2026).
**Colorado:** notice and disclosure duties for AI in consequential decisions start January 1, 2027.
**Texas, California and New York City** also regulate AI in hiring. Check your state.
